episodes.title: Car Service
episodes.logline: Move-in day at Whitlock: Cal Whitaker arrives alone in a hired car, and by sunset he's at a party on Elm Row with his last name chanted across the lawn.
episodes.recap: Cal Whitaker arrived at Whitlock alone in a hired car, his father's regrets delivered by assistant, and answered with a cheerful, perfectly smooth text. On the Quad he was adopted by Dev Okafor's family, hid Priya Raman from her mother in a closet, and let her read a single line from a notebook no one else had seen. He introduced himself to Herald reporter Nora Castellanos as 'Cal Whitaker, like the building,' offered her coffee, and was shot down. After building a crooked loft bed with Dev, the two traded polite lies, and Cal had dinner with the Okafors at Dot's, where he bought a fake Vermont license from a teenage busboy. At Kappa Lambda's Sunset on the Lawn he flirted hard with Margaux Vance, told her the truth about his father's absence, and climbed a keg table to toast that absent father to two hundred phones. Instead of answering Priya's late-night text, he followed Margaux to the roof, kissed her, turned off her phone as her mother kept calling, and spent the night with her, on one condition: nobody knows. At 1:14 a.m. his father finally texted, pleased with the video, and Cal promised to rush the Rho and got a 'Proud of you' for it. Dev found him in the hallway, and Cal told him the truth. By two a.m. Nora's story was live and Cal was starting a new notebook.

episodes.title: Two Truths and a Lie
episodes.logline: Orientation week: a poet appoints himself Cal's keeper, an anonymous account starts posting the third floor's secrets, and the oldest house on Elm Row sends its pledge master to collect a promise.
episodes.recap: Cal Whitaker woke up in Margaux Vance's Kappa Lambda sweatshirt and answered her ice-cold texts by waving at her entire sorority table. Simon Achterberg, the poet running orientation, caught Cal's tell on a staircase and adopted him as his ward; Cal agreed. When Dev's new roommate Yusuf questioned the housing lottery, Cal repeated the lie to Dev's face, and Dev covered for him again. Cal told Priya Raman he had promised not to say whose sweatshirt it was. At dawn an anonymous account, @lowell.three, posted his toast and the notebook line Priya had read aloud. Cal joked about it online, then held Priya instead of accusing her, wrote the true story of his mother's Maine weekend in the placement exam, and signed it with his real name. He gave Nora Castellanos 'No comment.' Brooks Hadley III, the Rho's pledge master, asked if he could swim. Cal made a joke, then hit back when Brooks sneered at Dev. He kissed Margaux on the Kappa back stairs rather than answer another question about his father. On Thursday he skipped his friends' trip under the school for the Rho's Legacy Dinner, roasted Brooks to his face, photographed an empty oval in a 1991 composite and dove off the Rho dock to the buoy and back. At 1 a.m. he heard Priya in the bathroom, promised her an hour, and stayed with Margaux until dawn.

episodes.title: Add/Drop
episodes.logline: The weekend before classes, Cal's mail is going somewhere else, the third floor is auditioning, and the one professor who won't let him coast has already read the truest thing he's written.
